subject: Transitive dependency lineage and contractual controls — inventory ask
messages:
From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@novacare.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: vendor-security@novacare.com
Date: Sun, 17 Aug 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: transitive dependency lineage and controls mapping

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the intro earlier this week. As part of NovaCare's procurement security review, our security team needs a deeper view into third-party/software supply-chain exposure for any vendors that will be in our inference pipeline. Specifically we need: 

- A list of direct and transitive (runtime) third-party libraries and components used by the production inference image(s) that will be in scope for our SOC2 assessment.
- An SCA report or SBOM export (CSV or CycloneDX) that includes versions and license types.
- Mapping of the transitive components to contractual controls (i.e., which subprocessor or supplier is responsible for updates, patch cadence, and CVE triage ownership).
- Any compensating controls if we have binaries or closed-source components (signing, pinned digests, deployment isolation).

We appreciate if you can provide a first-pass artifact by EOD Wednesday (2025-08-20) ahead of our legal/procurement review. If parts of this are sensitive, let us know and we can accept redacted artifacts plus a short control statement.

Thanks,
Liam O'Connor
Senior Security Engineer, NovaCare
liam.oconnor@novacare.com
[attachment: procurement-checklist.pdf (PDF, 320KB)]

From: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
To: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@novacare.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 17 Aug 2025 11:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: transitive dependency lineage and controls mapping

Liam —

Thanks for the clear list. We're on it. Quick notes/plan from our side:

- Neha will pull the SBOM/SCA export from the build pipeline and run an additional transitive resolution to ensure we include runtime-only deps. Expecting CSV + CycloneDX formats.
- Marcus will map the high-risk transitive components (runtime native libraries, crypto, native acceleration kernels) back to the owning subprocessor or open-source project and document which team handles patching and CVE triage.
- We'll provide a brief controls mapping doc that ties each item to our contract clauses or operational compensating controls (e.g., signed container digests, deployment-only read-only volumes, ephemeral key rotation).

Timeline: preliminary SBOM + SCA PDF by Tue 2025-08-19 EOD; full mapping and transitive graph by Wed 2025-08-20 EOD. If you need an earlier snapshot or partial redaction, say the word and we can expedite a redacted SBOM first.

Attaching an internal checklist for how we'll format the deliverables.

Best,
Stephanie Nguyen
Senior Manager, Security & Trust, Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai
[attachment: sbom_export_2025-08-17.csv (CSV, 1.1MB)]

From: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>
To: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@novacare.com>
Cc: marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 18 Aug 2025 08:37:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: transitive dependency lineage and controls mapping

Hi all —

Delivered the initial artifacts as discussed: attached SCA PDF from our CI pipeline and a raw SBOM export. Notes:

- sbom_export_2025-08-17.csv contains package, version, license, and source repo URL. We include a column "runtime=true" where the component is loaded at inference runtime (vs. build-only).
- sca-deps-report-2025-08-16.pdf includes the dependency tree and flagged CVEs with current severity and whether we've applied mitigations.
- transitive-deps-graph-2025-08-17.svg is a high-level graph mapping leaf components to owning teams or subsystems.

A few callouts:
- There are three transitive native libs (libfastops.so versions 1.x, 2.x, and an experimental 3.0) that are bundled by a third-party kernel vendor (KernelAccel Inc.). Per contract KernelAccel is responsible for security patches; Redwood performs runtime hardening and CVE monitoring. 
- For closed-source accelerator blobs we maintain pinned digests in our image registry and sign all released images with our KMS-backed keys.
- Where we rely on widely-used OSS (e.g., tokenizers, JSON parsers), we apply weekly SCA scans and triage via our vulnerabilities pipeline (JIRA SUP-3421).

If you want, Marcus can produce a short two-column mapping: "component -> contractual owner / remediation SLA" so legal/procurement has a clear line item by vendor.

Cheers,
Neha Kapoor
Security Engineer, Redwood Inference
neha_kapoor@redwood.ai
[attachments: sca-deps-report-2025-08-16.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB); transitive-deps-graph-2025-08-17.svg (SVG, 420KB)]

From: Liam O'Connor <liam.oconnor@novacare.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>
Cc: neha_kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>, marcus_lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, vendor-security@novacare.com
Date: Tue, 19 Aug 2025 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: transitive dependency lineage and controls mapping

Stephanie / Neha / Marcus —

Thanks for the quick turnaround and thorough artifacts. This looks good and addresses most of our procurement questions. A couple of follow-ups from our side: 

- Could you provide the two-column "component -> contractual owner / remediation SLA" mapping you mentioned for the legal team? It doesn't need to be exhaustive, just the top 25 components by criticality.
- For the KernelAccel native libs, can you confirm the current patch SLA in writing (we'll reference it in the contract appendix)?

If you can share the two-column mapping and a short statement on KernelAccel's SLA by EOD Thu (2025-08-21), procurement can move this to final review.

Appreciate the transparency — this helps speed things up on our side.

Best,
Liam
Senior Security Engineer, NovaCare
liam.oconnor@novacare.com
